page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring AMD hardware. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance includes 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics acceleration is provided by four AMD Radeon Pro V520 GPUs, which supply a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of 2400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs. The instance exhibits poor single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core and parallel capabilities are stronger, with the passmark CPU score, extended instructions, and encryption tests all ranking in the top 25%. Ray tracing performance is also strong, placing in the top 25% of Geekbench tests. Memory bandwidth and database operations score in the average and strong tiers respectively, while large-model LLM inference, such as text generation on a 70B model, is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.16xlarge offers a dense allocation of AMD GPUs and local NVMe storage relative to its resource class, making it a viable option for workloads that can leverage multi-GPU setups without requiring top-tier single-core CPU speeds. Appropriate workloads include graphics-intensive applications, ray tracing, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services g4ad.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and a 3.0 GHz clock speed. The hardware configuration includes 256 GB of DDR4 memory, four AMD Radeon Pro V520 GPUs with 32 GB of total VRAM, and 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network performance is established at a 25 Gbps baseline. Benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff: single-core CPU performance is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core execution, ray tracing, and encryption capabilities are strong, placing in the top 25%. This resource profile is suited for graphics-intensive applications, database operations, and multi-threaded processing tasks that benefit from local NVMe storage and parallel GPU acceleration.
